classification.reason: Request is a scientific goal or asks for planning without a concrete workflow.

plan.goal: Generate hotspot-directed binder candidates against the provided target protein, rank them after refolding and QC, and return one top binder sequence aimed at the specified site.
assumptions: Use the validated `target_sequence_binder_design_round` workflow because the request provides a target sequence and an explicit target-site residue list for hotspot-directed binder design.
Interpret the target binding-site residues as 1-indexed positions on target chain `A`: [25,35,36,39,40,72,73,76,128,132].
Use a 70-residue binder to give PXDesign enough interface area to cover a spatially clustered but sequence-dispersed epitope on this uncharacterized target.

Select the final binder from ranked candidates by preferring designs predicted to contact at least 5 of the 10 specified hotspot residues and rejecting designs whose interface is shifted to a different surface.
Provider selected a workflow template by reference; expanded it to the validated local workflow descriptor.

workflow_plan.name: target_sequence_binder_design_round
workflow_plan.description: Fold a target sequence, generate hotspot-directed binders with PXDesign pipeline mode, analyze, QC, and rank candidates.

success_criteria.final_output_format:
Reason: <brief design rationale>
Answer: <designed protein sequence using amino acid letters only>
success_criteria.site_specificity: Return a binder predicted to engage the intended hotspot surface rather than an alternative face of the target.
success_criteria.ranking_rule: Choose the highest-ranked binder that passes refold/QC checks and satisfies the hotspot-contact criterion in the predicted complex.
